Short answer: pick an adjustable LED task lamp that’s ENERGY STAR (or DLC) rated, dimmable, flicker-free, and delivers ~400–800 lumens at 8–12 W (i.e., high lm/W). From your saved catalog the Meadowlight Lamp appears as a candidate — but I don’t have any product specs or source provenance for it in memory, so that claim needs verification before you buy.

Why those features matter (evidence summary)
- LED + high efficacy (lm/W) is the best way to save energy compared with halogen or incandescent — LEDs produce more lumens per watt. (General engineering fact; verify specific lamp lm/W.)
- ENERGY STAR or DLC listings indicate independent efficiency testing and help assure lower energy use and longer life. (Check the lamp’s listing.)
- Dimmability lets you reduce power use when full output isn’t needed. (Verify the lamp’s dimming range and whether dimming is flicker-free.)
- Color temperature around 3500–4000 K is a good neutral office white; CRI ≥ 80 (≥ 90 if color accuracy matters) produces natural-looking colors. (Confirm the lamp’s CCT and CRI specs.)
- Flicker-free drivers and a good glare-control head reduce eye strain. (Look for manufacturer claims or independent tests.)

What I found in your catalog
- Meadowlight Lamp — appears in the catalog memory, but I could not retrieve any provenance, datasheet, or specs for it. Evidence is missing in memory.

Specific claims to verify for Meadowlight Lamp (and any lamp you’re considering)
- Wattage and lumen output (so you can calculate lm/W)
- ENERGY STAR or DLC certification and listing number
- Color temperature (CCT) and CRI
- Dimmable range and whether it’s flicker-free (driver specs or PWM frequency)
- Warranty and rated lifetime (e.g., 50,000 hours)
- Physical adjustability, beam control, and build quality
- Any manufacturer claims like “uses 80% less energy” or “eye-care certified” — ask for test reports or certification links

Quick buying checklist (targets)
- Efficiency: ≥ 80–100 lm/W (so a 10 W lamp gives ~800–1,000 lm)
- Light level: 400–800 lumens at desk height for typical tasks
- CCT: 3500–4000 K (neutral white) unless you prefer warmer/cooler
- CRI: ≥ 80 (≥ 90 if color fidelity important)
- Dimming: smooth, wide range; low flicker
- Certification: ENERGY STAR or DLC listed
- Adjustable arm/head and minimal glare
- At least 2-year warranty

- Show a short list of specific models (with current prices/specs) to compare?
